title: The Core Mass Function across Galactic Environments. II. Infrared Dark Cloud Clumps
question: What is the core mass function in IRDC clumps, and does it differ from the Salpeter IMF and from the more evolved G286 protocluster?

data.bands: 1.3 mm continuum, continuum band centred at 231.55 GHz
data.arrays: 12 m array only, 29 antennas; no ACA

what.value: Dust opacity 0.899 cm2/g (moderately coagulated thin ice mantle model)

evidence.quote: moderately coagulated thin ice mantle model of Ossenkopf & Henning 1994
Paper I also presented results for 1.0$''$ resolution and with a noise level of 0.45 mJy beam$^{-1}$

recipe.method: Compare ALMA flux above 3 sigma and BGPS flux in 27'' aperture, scaling BGPS to 231.6 GHz
astrodendro on images before primary-beam correction; leaves are cores; within primary beam FWHM; clumpfind as alternative
key_parameters: trunk 4 sigma, branch +1 sigma, min leaf area 0.5 beam

recipe.method: Optically thin dust emission, Sigma_mm formula
Insert artificial Gaussian cores (3 at a time, 50 repeats, 150 experiments per mass) over 10^-1 to 10^1.2 Msun, rerun dendrogram

recipe.goal: Fit CMF power law and compare
recipe.method: Least-squares in log dN/dlogM with Poisson errors, and MLE (Newman 2005), five bins per dex; KS tests vs Salpeter and G286

evidence.quote: Overall we have identified 107 cores in these images.

answer_key.quantity: Median flux recovery fraction vs BGPS

evidence.quote: we derive a median flux recovery fraction of 0.19 $\pm$ 0.02

answer_key.quantity: Combined true CMF alpha, M>=0.79 Msun (simple)

evidence.quote: power law indices for $M>0.79\:M_\odot$ of $\alpha=0.50\pm0.10$, $0.49\pm0.09$ and $0.86\pm0.11$, respectively

answer_key.quantity: Combined true CMF alpha, M>=1.26 Msun (simple)

evidence.quote: then we derive $\alpha=0.70\pm0.13$ for the true CMF
The masses range from $0.261 M_{\odot}$ to $178\:M_{\odot}$

score_reason: Public data and clear analysis recipe with a core table, but imaging steps and some parameters are inherited or unstated.
